verdict.rationale: A hands-on user says Solid is small and easy to inject into other pages, and the README says it can author custom elements, a native way to embed interactive components in existing HTML. However, no first-party docs describe mounting into an existing server-rendered page; the documented SSR and progressive hydration cover Solid's own server rendering, not arbitrary existing HTML. missing for 10: first-party docs on mounting or islands-style embedding into existing server-rendered pages, a documented no-build or script-tag setup, and more than one independent hands-on report.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drop the framework into an existing server-rendered HTML page and render interactive components without rewriting the whole page

citations.quote: Uses Solid as a go-to for data viz because it is small and easy to inject into other pages.
Web component friendly and can author custom elements
Solid's bare-metal, minimal abstractions give you direct access to the DOM
